name: SST25VF080B-50-4I-S2AE
title: 8 Mbit SPI serial flash, 2.7 V to 3.6 V
summary: The SST25VF080B is an 8 Mbit (1 Mbyte) flash memory with a four-wire SPI port (modes 0 and 3) that reads and writes from a single 2.7 V to 3.6 V supply. The array erases in 4 Kbyte sectors or in 32 Kbyte and 64 Kbyte blocks, programs a byte at a time or two bytes at a time in auto address increment (AAI) mode, and is guarded by block-protection bits in its STATUS register and a write-protect pin. The read command 03H runs to 25 MHz and the high-speed read 0BH to 50 MHz, or 66 MHz with VDD from 3.0 V. It comes in 8-lead PDIP, 8-lead SOIC (200 mil), 8-contact WSON (6 mm x 5 mm) and 16-bump XFBGA packages, in commercial and industrial temperature grades.

pins.name: CE#
pins.function: Chip enable, active low. A falling edge selects the device and starts a command; it stays low for the whole command sequence.

pins.name: SO
pins.function: Serial data output, changing on the falling edge of SCK. With EBSY set it reports busy (low) or ready (high) as RY/BY# during AAI programming.

pins.name: WP#
pins.function: Write-protect input. Low enables the lock-down action of the BPL bit in the STATUS register; high disables it.

pins.name: SI
pins.function: Serial data input for commands, addresses and data, sampled on the rising edge of SCK.

pins.name: SCK
pins.function: Serial clock. Inputs are taken on its rising edge and output data moves out on its falling edge.

pins.name: HOLD#
pins.function: Hold, active low. Pauses a serial transfer in progress without resetting the device.

pins.name: exposed pad
pins.function: WSON only. Connected inside to the back of the die, and perhaps to some VSS leads. It may be soldered down; VSS is the suggested connection. Joining it to any other potential can short or upset the device.

operation.text: The array is laid out as uniform 4 Kbyte erasable sectors, overlaid by 32 Kbyte blocks and 64 Kbyte erasable blocks. Addresses run from 00000H to FFFFFH.

The bus is CE#, SCK, SI and SO. SPI mode 0 (0,0) and mode 3 (1,1) both work; they differ only in where SCK rests while the master is idle and no data moves: low in mode 0, high in mode 3. In either mode SI is sampled on the rising SCK edge and SO changes after the falling edge.

With CE# low, HOLD# pauses a sequence without resetting the clock count. Hold begins when a falling HOLD# edge meets SCK low and ends when a rising HOLD# edge meets SCK low; an edge that comes while SCK is high takes effect at the next SCK low. In hold SO floats and SI and SCK are ignored (either level). Taking CE# high during hold resets the internal logic. The device stays held while HOLD# is low; to continue, HOLD# goes high with CE# low.

Bits BP3 to BP0 and BPL in the STATUS register protect the array and the register itself. WP# low turns on the lock-down action of BPL: when BPL is 1, WRSR is ignored. WP# high disables the lock-down and BPL no longer matters.

While an internal program or erase runs, reading the STATUS register is the only access allowed, used to see when it finishes. BUSY is 1 while an internal erase or program is running and 0 when the device is ready. WEL shows the write enable latch: at 1 the device accepts program and erase commands, at 0 it rejects them. WEL clears itself at power-up and on completion of WRDI, Byte Program, AAI programming (finished or stopped at the highest unprotected address), Sector Erase, Block Erase, Chip Erase and WRSR.

BP3 to BP0 set how much of the array is shielded from program and erase. WRSR can change them while WP# is high or BPL is 0. Chip Erase runs only with all BP bits at 0. After power-up BP2, BP1 and BP0 come up at 1, protecting all blocks, BP3 at 0, the AAI bit reads Byte Program mode, and BPL is 0. With WP# low, setting BPL to 1 freezes BPL and BP3 to BP0.

Commands, addresses and data are each 8-bit bus cycles, most significant bit first, taken on rising SCK edges after CE# falls. WREN must come before Byte Program, AAI programming, Sector Erase, Block Erase, Chip Erase and WRSR. CE# must go low before a command and high after its last bit, except for Read, Read-ID and RDSR. CE# rising before the last bit of a bus cycle aborts the command and returns the device to standby.
Read runs to 25 MHz: 03H, then the 24-bit address [A23-A0], then data from that address for as long as CE# stays low. The address counts up and wraps from FFFFFH to 00000H.

High-Speed Read runs to 66 MHz: 0BH, the 24-bit address, one dummy byte (eight clocks at either level), then data streaming from the address with the same count-up and wrap from FFFFFH to 00000H, until CE# rises.

After WREN, send 02H, the 24-bit address and one data byte MSb first, then raise CE# to start the self-timed write. The target byte must be erased (FFH); a write into a protected area does nothing. Completion is found by polling BUSY or by waiting TBP.

AAI writes two bytes per step without resending the address. After WREN, send ADH, the 24-bit address and two data bytes: the first lands at [A23-A1] with A0 = 0, the second with A0 = 1. Raise CE# to start; once not busy, send ADH and the next two bytes, and so on. The range must be erased (FFH) and must not be protected, or the command is ignored. The address does not wrap once the highest unprotected address is reached. While in AAI with software detection only ADH, WRDI and RDSR are accepted; with hardware detection only ADH and WRDI. To finish, check busy, then send WRDI (software mode) or WRDI followed by DBSY (hardware mode).

Three ways show when each AAI step ends: poll BUSY with RDSR, wait TBP, or read SO as a hardware ready flag. For the hardware method send EBSY (70H) before the AAI command; then whenever CE# goes low during programming SO shows 0 for busy and 1 for ready, and SO floats again when CE# rises. To leave this mode send WRDI (clearing WEL and AAI) and then DBSY (80H).

After WREN, Sector Erase is 20H plus a 24-bit address; bits AMS-A12 pick the 4 Kbyte sector, which is set to FFH. 32-Kbyte Block Erase is 52H and 64-Kbyte Block Erase is D8H, each with a 24-bit address whose upper bits pick the block. Other address bits may be at either level. CE# rises to start the self-timed erase; poll BUSY or wait TSE or TBE. An erase aimed at a protected area is ignored.
After WREN, 60H or C7H with CE# then raised sets every bit to FFH. It is ignored if any part of the array is protected. Poll BUSY or wait TCE.

RDSR works at any time, including during a program or erase, so BUSY can be checked before the next command. CE# goes low before 05H and stays low while the register is read; the register repeats until CE# rises.

WREN (06H) sets WEL to 1 and must precede every program or erase. It can also enable WRSR, in which case WEL clears on the rising CE# that ends WRSR. WRDI (04H) clears WEL and AAI, blocking new writes; it does not stop a program in progress, which may run for up to TBP. CE# must go high to execute either command.

EWSR arms WRSR so that the register can be altered; WRSR must follow straight after it. The two-command pairing guards the register against accidental writes. CE# goes low before EWSR and high to execute it.

WRSR, preceded by EWSR or WREN, writes BP3 to BP0 and BPL; CE# rises to execute it. With WP# low and BPL at 1 the command has no effect. With WP# low, BPL can be set from 0 to 1 but not cleared. With WP# high, or BPL at 0 before the CE# rising edge that ends WRSR, every writable bit can change, so one WRSR can set BPL and the BP bits together.
After 9FH the device sends BFH (manufacturer), 25H (SPI serial flash) and 8EH (SST25VF080B) on SO. CE# rising ends the output at any point.

A backward-compatible identification command, recommended as the default ID read in a design that uses several SPI serial flash versions. Send 90H or ABH and a 24-bit address; address 00000H gives BFH and 00001H gives 8EH, and the output alternates between the two until CE# rises.

All functions and DC figures hold for a VDD ramp faster than 1 V per 100 ms (0 V to 3.0 V in under 300 ms). Between VDD reaching its minimum and the end of TPU-READ or TPU-WRITE the chip must not be selected, since commands may be refused or misread; after that the device is fully accessible.

Each signal has an inner bump and an outer bump joined inside the package. The outer bumps serve for mechanical support and are not electrically tested. For footprint compatibility with other Z-Scale packages all eight inner bumps must be connected. Underfill is recommended for solder-joint reliability.
